I'll start by reading the benchmark instructions and the task list so I know exactly what to implement.Reslil’s operator grouping and integer division are unusual, so I’ll probe those with the toolchain before writing the solutions.The language matches the reference on floor division and right-to-left operators. Next I’ll implement every task and test it against that behavior.The solutions are in place. I’ll check them against independent expected results, including the awkward arithmetic cases.All 17 tasks are solved in `solutions/` and checked against the toolchain, including floor division, Gregorian weekdays, big-integer arithmetic, Game of Life, toward-zero RPN, and word-frequency order.

What tripped me up was that every binary operator has the same precedence and groups right to left, so `2 * 3 + 4` is `2 * (3 + 4)` and `10 - 4 - 3` is `10 - (4 - 3)`. Comparisons mixed with `dilisyo` need parentheses for the same reason. Integer division rounds toward negative infinity, which makes `-7 / 2` equal `-4` with remainder `1`. That matched the floor-division and rotation tasks, while the RPN calculator wanted truncation toward zero and had to be rebuilt from the floor quotient. `dilisyo` and `emsoulve` always evaluate both operands, so a bounds check cannot share an expression with an index. Lists compare by identity, `xs[i][j]` can be read, and assigning through two indexes is a syntax error. There is no split or character-code builtin, and `<-` is one token, so a comparison with a negative number needs a space. The reference note that `1 + 2 + "x"` prints `3x` also disagreed with the toolchain, which prints `12x` under that same right-to-left grouping.
